newsitem.title: USA: U.S. money managers less defensive on US debt-MCM.
newsitem.headline: U.S. money managers less defensive on US debt-MCM.

text.p: U.S. fixed-income managers slightly increased the durations of their U.S. debt portfolios over the past week, according to an MCM MoneyWatch Inc survey.
"Cash seems to have been put to work in the latest week's rallies, which explains why durations rose," according to MCM first vice president and senior economist Astrid Adolfson.
In the week ended April 21, the survey showed durations as a percentage of benchmark rose to 106.4 percent from 106.3 percent the week before.
A portfolio's duration represents its average maturity and is used by portfolio managers to calculate exposure to risk.
In the "next likely move" category, portfolio managers representing 42 percent of total assets in the survey said they would "buy," compared with 46 percent the prior week.
Strategists leaning toward "sell" fell to 6.0 percent, down from 8.0 percent in the week ended April 14.
Fifty-two percent of managers said they were "neutral" on the market, up from 46 percent a week ago.
Cash as a percentage of assets slipped to 3.27 percent, against 3.36 percent registered the previous week.

The survey showed 33 percent of investors polled overweighted the 10-plus years duration sector, up from 31 percent the previous week, while 9.0 percent underweighted it. The remaining 58 percent were "neutral."
In the five- to 10-year duration sector, 47 percent of investors polled said they overweighted the securities and 15 percent underweighted them.

Separately, almost all of the respondents in the survey said they expect the Federal Reserve to raise short-term interest rates by 25 basis points at the Federal Open Market Committee on May 20, MCM said.
The survey included 38 domestic participants who manage about $110 billion in fixed-income assets. The poll is conducted weekly by MCM and usually is released on Tuesday.
